paper_title: On the Size of Good-For-Games Rabin Automata and Its Link with the Memory in Muller Games
classifications: Theory of computation → Automata over infinite objects
source_locator: Explicit open question on PDF page 14
statement: ▶ Remark 20 (Optimisation on the number of Rabin pairs). An important parameter in the study of Rabin automata is the number of Rabin pairs used. The automaton presented in this Section uses a number of Rabin pairs that equals the number of round nodes in the Zielonka tree. This can be improved by using only the round nodes in the Zielonka directed acyclic graph (obtained from the tree by merging nodes with the same labels). However, even this latter option is not always optimal and we conjecture that minimising the number of Rabin pairs without increasing the size of the automaton is NP-complete.

However, even this latter option is not always optimal and we conjecture that minimising the number of Rabin pairs without increasing the size of the automaton is NP-complete. 4 GFG Rabin automata recognising Muller conditions can be exponentially more succinct than deterministic ones in number of states On his PhD Thesis [23, 24], Kopczyński raised the question of whether the general and the chromatic memory requirements of winning conditions always coincide. By Theorem 5 and [10, Theorem 28], in the case of Muller conditions, this question is equivalent to the following: Is there a Muller language L such that minimal GFG Rabin automata recognising L are strictly smaller than deterministic Rabin automata for L?
